journey: CH-14 Use a skill by name (`use <name>`), and a skill that is switched off
title: On a default install, typing 'use <skill>' in Chat does nothing and says nothing, because skill instructions in Chat are off by a setting no screen exposes
trigger: Default install. Send 'use debugging skill to look at this' (an enabled, callable skill), 'use genie-npu-ir20 for this' (enabled, not callable), 'use nosuchskill please', '@skill debugging explain this' (and 'use debugging' in the verification workspace). Then open Capabilities > Skills.

actual: All five turns answered like any other turn: no chip, no message. The skill does not load because the path that loads skill instructions runs only when feature flag chatSkillInstructionsV1Enabled is true (chat-feature-admission-service.ts:171; the `use <name>` reader callable-skill-activation.ts:157 is reached only through that branch). The flag defaults to false (config.ts:1535, feature-flags.ts:57 and :154) and a read-only GET of the sandbox's /api/v1/settings returned features.chatSkillInstructionsV1Enabled = false. No Cockpit screen sets it (git grep finds the flag only in config, Gateway and a shared API type, and the Settings route schema at dashboard.ts:266), and Capabilities > Skills still lists the skill as on and callable, so an operator following the `use <name>` guidance cannot make it work from any screen or learn why. The Gateway trace recorded activated_skill_count 0 for every turn, which is what flag-off produces (chat-turn-runtime-decisions.ts:48). No Chat UI code shows an activated or refused skill either, so even with the flag on there is no chip (git grep). A switched-off skill is dropped silently in the Gateway (chat-skill-selection-runtime.ts:74). Not run live: switching a skill off. Off by default by design (docs/1_0_CONTRACT.md:7), but Capabilities promises the Chat half: SkillPanelSwitch.tsx:13-14 says 'Paused skills are used when you name them in Chat', and the install approval reads 'Lets the AI use <name> in new chats.' (skill-install-view.ts:153). Reading skills from Chat ('skills.read') sits behind another default-off flag.

title: When connecting an MCP server fails, the row says 'open it to see why' but the panel shows no reason unless Settings > Technical details is on, and nothing says so
trigger: Advanced setup > MCP servers > Inspect the server > Review connection > Connect reviewed server, on a host where the connection fails (here the sandbox has no OS keychain: 'OS keychain backend is unavailable on this host'). Then read the Connectors row and open its panel, with the Settings 'Technical details' preference at its default (off).
expected: The panel shows the reason, or says where it is ('turn on Technical details in Settings > Appearance').
actual: The Gateway recorded the cause as the server's last error for any connect failure (reviewedConnectFailure stores the cause's own words, secret-redacted; here 'Reviewed MCP connection did not complete: OS keychain backend is unavailable on this host'). The row reads 'Not working - Stopped working; open it to see why - Try again'. The panel reads only 'Not working. Stopped working. Try again'. The reason is rendered only as 'Last error' inside a Technical details block, which exists only when the Settings > Appearance 'Technical details' checkbox is on; it is off by default (showTechnicalDetails false), and the extra sentence 'The last error is under Technical details.' that points at it is also printed only when the preference is on. With the default, the row's promise cannot be kept and no screen says a preference would show the reason. The cause in this run was the sandbox's missing keychain, but the gap holds for any connect failure. Not re-run with the preference on (Last error not seen live). Separately, after the 500 the inspection said 'MCP connection outcome is unconfirmed. Further changes to this server are locked for this app session; inspect its current owner state.' and Review connection and Review disconnect were greyed; seen once, after a 500 in the sandbox, cause not isolated. Correction: Technical details is on by default only in Advanced mode (ui-preferences.tsx:80 and :270-285 derive it from the mode); Simple mode, the default, hides the reason.

title: In every project conversation the composer shows 'Approval mode unavailable' with a Retry button that can never work when the Gateway is in its default no-login mode
trigger: Gateway auth mode none, which is the shipped default (config/goatcitadel.example.json auth.mode none, allowLoopbackBypass false; the packaged Windows desktop launcher sets only GOATCITADEL_HOME, GOATCITADEL_APP_DIR and GOATCITADEL_DESKTOP_HOST, so it stays in mode none; goatcitadel up and pnpm dev default to none too). Open any conversation that belongs to a project (for example the seeded 'Release readiness review'). The row 'Approval mode unavailable / Retry' appears above the composer; Retry repeats the same request.
expected: Either the managed-project 'Use Auto mode' control, or nothing; if the control cannot be offered on this connection the row says why (for example that it needs a signed-in local connection) instead of offering a Retry.
actual: GET /api/v1/chat/sessions/<id>/approval-mode answers 403 'Chat approval mode requires a local operator connection.' even from curl straight to 127.0.0.1 (no proxy, no cross-origin). In auth mode none the actor source is 'none' (plugins/auth.ts:180-182 returns there, before the loopback-bypass check is reached), and directLocal is never granted for that source, so the route refuses every call. This looks like a deliberate security rule (mode none cannot prove the caller is local); no document states it, and whether none-mode installs should be able to use Auto mode is a product decision, not decided here. What is defective regardless is the presentation: the row says 'unavailable' with a Retry that cannot succeed, gives no reason and no pointer to Settings › Access, and the browser console logs a 403 per load. For an operator whose goal is Auto mode or Managed files there is no path on screen. Who sees it: every mode-none install (packaged desktop, goatcitadel up, pnpm dev; the dev supervisor defaults to mode none, so its loopback bypass is not reached), in any conversation that belongs to a project. Docker (docker-compose.yaml:74-76 sets token mode with loopback bypass false) and proxied or remote setups likely see it as well because the request does not arrive as a direct loopback connection (unverified, not run). Token or basic mode with a direct loopback client does not get the 403 (code only, not run: the auth mode may not be changed in this review). While the row is shown the composer loses only the 'Use Auto mode' / 'Managed files' controls; sending, attachments, model and web options still work (checked live). Confirmed by the token-mode comparison (Task 13b, tk-ch-1-project.json): a project conversation in token mode shows 'Standard approvals / Use Auto mode', Auto mode turns on with no dialog and Managed files opens; mode-none installs therefore lose both. Settings > Access in mode none does not mention it (st-5-access.png); it is the natural place for the pointer. Whether mode-none installs should get Auto mode and Managed files is listed as a design decision.

A drive path is not a documented capability: the local-folder import copies the folder into the workspace and stores a workspace-relative path (chat-project-service.ts:90-146, relative path at line 109). The plausible risk, not tried: on Windows path.resolve(workspaceRoot, project.workspacePath) (chat-workbench-service.ts:1029, :1610) returns the drive path itself, so later path resolution points outside the workspace root; whoever owns path safety should look at it.
